_comment: Who sent a chat message, as both plugins put it in trigger.sender. `chat` is a direct message or a group (any group chat, server channel or thread); `owner` says the sender is the host's owner (OpenClaw's owner flag; on Hermes, individually on <PLATFORM>_ALLOWED_USERS or GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS). Both plugins must give the same `relation` and the same answer to whether the basis carries `group_chat`. The owner in a group stays the owner, with basis group_chat; everyone else there is other. `trusted_user` lists the sender as a trusted user and `trusted_chat` marks the chat as trusted; a trusted sender is `trusted` with the basis `allowlist` names (`plugin_allowlist:sender` or `plugin_allowlist:chat`), and stays below the owner: the owner in a trusted chat is still the owner. A direct chat is never a trusted chat. `trusted_server` names a Discord server id the owner trusts (`discord:server:<id>`); `server` is the server the host reports for the turn (none when absent); `chat_id` overrides the chat's id and `trusted_chat_id` names a trusted chat by id. A trusted server covers every channel and thread in it (`plugin_allowlist:chat`), never a direct chat, and a chat id is never matched against a server entry or a server id against a chat entry.
